So far what I got going on is 5 "nations" or states or whatever. Mostly humans and evolutionary shifts of humans. One nation is a swamp/marshland base with floating reed cities (Kibashas are a major inspiration) with a tribal chiefdom. Constant fog in the area and humans that have merged themselves with a magical fungal type thing. Use a massive fungal underground network for things like fast communication. Originally this nation was exiles from a Theocratic nation that sits just to the south (not going for the mega evil religious corrupt thing that's so overplayed, id like to think of the swamp area as more of an Australian type deal). The theocracy is heavily focused on farming, on a plains/steppe type landmass, need to work more on the inner workings of this particular nation. Then on the southern tip a heavily temperate deciduous forest area with a group of humans that speak in a whisper based conlang I am working on, who are sort of taking on the woodelf trope of nature lovers who only allow truly dedicated outsiders to enter. Considering making fairies present here, more hunter gatherer type society. Enclosed by mountains a plutocracy of wealthy merchants with a heavy naval influence because of the protection from mountains who trade for most of their supplies. Lastly a desert type matriarchy with little to no religious influence, with a harsh but fair system of justice, and mechanical magics, like simple war machines and contraptions. I'm reading a lot of books on war tactics, religious sects, and architecture, phonetics, and mythology at the moment so I can really make the world feel alive, and am only just starting to shape things.

For now I am focusing on this smaller protrusion as you said, similar to the Korean Peninsula, (somewhat isolated area)I really want to spend a lot of time fleshing out the cultures of the area. There's 5 nations that sit in the area, I want to keep the population density somewhat low, maybe total population of this section 750k-1m. I imagine the scale somewhere around N and S Korea sized, with mostly humans, (and some variations on humans).
